findings.title: SQL injection via string-built query
findings.severity_rationale: HTTP request input flows directly into the SQL text with no authentication required, so an attacker can read (or alter) any data the database user can access.

evidence.query_code: sql = f"SELECT id, title FROM documents WHERE is_public = 1 AND title LIKE '%{term}%'"

findings.explanation: In route /search, the SQL statement is built with f-string and then passed to execute(). Any quote or SQL keyword inside the interpolated value becomes part of the query itself instead of being treated as data.
findings.impact: An attacker can change the meaning of the query, for example turning a filtered search into 'return every row' or appending a UNION SELECT that reads other tables such as user credentials.
findings.remediation: Keep the SQL text constant and pass values separately as bound parameters, e.g. db.execute("... WHERE title LIKE ?", (f"%{term}%",)). The database driver then treats the value strictly as data.
findings.detection_method: Python AST analysis: located a DB-API execute() call whose first argument (directly or via a local variable) is an f-string / concatenation / %-format / .format() containing SQL keywords; traced interpolated variables one assignment back to request input.

findings.title: Broken access control (IDOR) on object lookup
findings.severity_rationale: Any caller can read another user's private record by changing an identifier in the URL. No special privileges or user interaction are needed and confidentiality impact is high; rated HIGH rather than CRITICAL because it exposes records one at a time and does not allow arbitrary query execution.

evidence.lookup_code: doc = query_one("SELECT id, owner_id, title, body, is_public FROM documents WHERE id = ?", (doc_id,))

findings.explanation: Route /documents/<int:doc_id> loads a record using the client-supplied 'doc_id' value (line 85) and returns it without checking whether the current user is allowed to see that record. An access-check helper (can_view_document) exists in this module but this route never calls it.
findings.impact: Insecure Direct Object Reference: a student can read another student's private documents simply by iterating document IDs, and anonymous callers can read private data.
findings.remediation: After loading the record, enforce a server-side authorisation rule (owner, assigned teacher, or public) and return 403 when it fails. Never rely on the client to only request IDs it is allowed to see.
findings.detection_method: Python AST analysis: found a route with a URL path parameter that is passed into a data lookup, with no access-check helper call, authorisation decorator, ownership comparison or ownership-filtered query in the route body.

62d53f56-d543-4fb2-8dbe-1e7e84c13536.rationale: The SQL text is now a constant ("SELECT id, title FROM documents WHERE is_public = 1 AND title LIKE ?") and the 1 user-influenced value(s) are passed separately as bound parameters (f"%{term}%",). The database driver sends them as data, so quotes or SQL keywords in the input can no longer change the query. Wildcards that were part of the original string literal (e.g. % for LIKE) are moved into the parameter so search behaviour is unchanged.
